content: I'll start by reading the test image and the part index file simultaneously.

The test image shows a tomato stem/shoot with:
- Drooping/curling shoot tips (shepherd's crook appearance)
- Dark brown/black necrotic tissue at the stem base/node
- Shriveled, rotten-looking tissue at the junction
- Surrounding healthy green leaves

This is primarily a **stem** issue. Candidates from the stem part index: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Gray_Mold, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

Now I'll view one reference image from each of my top 4 candidates.
Bacterial Canker shows more vascular browning and leaf wilting. Let me check Gray_Mold next.
Gray Mold shows similar stem/node necrosis with wilting - the bottom-right panel matches well. Let me check Alternaria next.
Alternaria shows fruit rot and basal stem cankers - doesn't match well. Let me check Sclerotinia for my 4th view.

**Analysis Summary:**

- **Test image**: Two drooping/curling shoot tips (shepherd's crook) above a dark, shriveled necrotic node/junction. The affected tissue is dark brown-black with a rotted, collapsed appearance. Surrounding tissue is healthy green.

- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt**: Shows vascular browning and leaf margin necrosis — not the concentrated node rot seen here.
- **Gray_Mold**: The bottom-right panel (5573933) shows a stem node with dark necrotic tissue and drooping wilted shoots above it — **very close match** to the test image. Botrytis classically infects stem nodes causing "shepherd's crook" wilting of the tissues above.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Shows fruit blossom-end rot and basal stem cankers — doesn't match the node-level wilting pattern.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Shows bleached/white stem tissue and sclerotia — the stem appearance is quite different (paler, more bleached vs. dark necrotic).

The dark necrotic node lesion with drooping shoots above is most characteristic of **Gray_Mold** (Botrytis cinerea) infecting a stem node.
